newsitem.title: UK: UK shares end lower as market awaits word from Fed.
newsitem.headline: UK shares end lower as market awaits word from Fed.

text.p: ** UK shares end weaker, off day's lows, as the market
awaits word from the Fed after FOMC meeting today.
** Bank sector leads decline as institutions take profits.
** Legal & General jumps as BZW reiterates buy note.
** Carlton up after positive meetings with analysts.

"If we see 25 basis points, I think the market will breathe a sign of relief. Over 50 basis points, I think, will mean the top for both of these (UK and U.S.) markets," said UK equity strategist Scott Evan at UBS.
The FTSE 100 surged to a record of 3,994.1 only last Friday. But worries about higher interest rates took the wind out of the rally, traders said.
The Bank of England, meanwhile, left interest rates unchanged, as expected. UK monetary authorities met yesterday and signalled no change in policy in money markets this morning.
But the lack of a rate hike failed to support the FTSE.
"It was a political event," said Evan of the BoE's inaction.
A rate increase, he added, might be warranted given a stronger-than-expected 2.2 percent GDP growth in the second quyarter.
Worries about higher U.S. interest rates hit UK banking shares hardest. The bank sector, one of the best performing groups this year, tumbled, as institutions took profits, traders said.
HSBC Holdings, under the additional weight of a profit warning from the bank, closed 19-1/2p lower at 1183-1/2p.
Among other bank stocks, Standard Chartered fell 12p to 706-1/2p. Barclays eased 7p to 932-1/2p, and Natwest slipped 6p to 660-1/2p.

Shares in UK food retailers, which have underperformed the broad market, bucked the weaker tone. Shares in Tesco gained 2p to 303p after brokerage Kleinwort Benson reiterated its "buy" recommendation on the stock.
BZW, meanwhile, issued a buy note on Legal & General, sparking a 14-1/2p rally to 784-1/2p.
Shares in Rank Organisation stumbled 9-1/2p to 429-1/2p after the leisure group confirmed its bid for pubs operator Tom Cobleigh with an agreed deal at 240p per share.
Manchester United rose 7p to 453-1/2 after reports the company had received a takeover bid.
Shares in Carlton Communications jumped following a series of positive meetings with analysts, traders said. The shares closed up 14p to 486-1/2p.
-- Debra Sherman, London newsroom +44 171 542 4026
